# Forge

> Forge is an internet-native programming language implemented in Rust. HTTP client and server, SQLite/Postgres/MySQL, JSON, CSV, crypto, JWT, regex, filesystem, shell, and concurrency are built in, with no imports or packages. Source files use the `.fg` extension.

This file is the canonical, compact guide for AI models writing Forge. Every code block below was run on Forge v0.9.x with the default engine (`forge run file.fg`). Prefer the forms shown here.

Forge also has an optional "natural" syntax (`set x to 5`, `say`, `define`, `otherwise`, ...). It is sugar for the classic syntax below. Write classic syntax unless asked otherwise.

## Running

```
forge run app.fg                 # run (bytecode VM, the default engine)
forge --interp run app.fg        # tree-walking interpreter (reference semantics)
forge --jit run app.fg           # VM + Cranelift JIT for numeric functions
forge --allow-run run app.fg     # allow sh/run_command and other shell builtins
forge -e 'println(1 + 2)'        # evaluate inline
forge test                       # run @test functions in tests/*.fg
forge build --native app.fg      # native executable (also: fmt, new, lsp, add, install)
forge mcp --allow-net=api.x.com  # MCP server: AI agents run Forge in a deny-all sandbox
forge mcp serve tools.fg         # serve @tool functions as MCP tools
forge run --max-fuel 1000000 --max-memory 64MB f.fg  # deterministic step budget + memory cap ("fuel exhausted" / "memory limit exceeded", not catchable)
```

Engine flags go BEFORE the subcommand: `forge --interp run x.fg`, not `forge run x.fg --interp`. Operators: `+ - * / %`, `== != < <= > >=`, `&& || !`, `+=`.

## Values, variables, strings

```forge
let name = "Forge"            // immutable binding
let mut count = 0             // mutable binding
count += 1
count = count + 1
let pi = 3.14                 // Float
let ok = true                 // Bool
let nothing = null            // Null
let nums = [1, 2, 3]          // Array
let user = { name: "Ada", age: 36 }   // Object (string keys, insertion-ordered)
let pair = (1, "one")         // Tuple
println("Hello, {name}! count={count}")   // "{expr}" interpolates inside double-quoted strings
println(typeof(pi))           // Float
println(user.name)
println(nums[0])
println(len(nums))
println(str(42) + "!")
println(int("7") + 1)
println(10 / 4)               // 2 (Int / Int is integer division)
```

Types: `Int`, `Float`, `String`, `Bool`, `Null`, `Array`, `Object`, `Tuple`, plus `Set`, `Map`, `Result`, `Option`, structs and algebraic types. Annotations are optional: `let t: Int = 42`, `fn f(x: Int) -> String`. Comments are `//`. Triple-quoted `"""..."""` strings span lines.

## Type annotations and checking

Annotation syntax: `Int`, `[Int]`, `?String` (or `Option<String>`), `Result<Int, String>`, `Map<String, Int>`, `Set<Int>`, `(Int, String)`, `fn(Int, Int) -> Bool`, `Any`, user structs/types, generics `fn first<T>(xs: [T]) -> T`, `struct Box<T> { value: T }`.

```forge
fn apply(f: fn(Int) -> Int, x: Int) -> Int { return f(x) }
let twice: fn(Int) -> Int = fn(n) { n * 2 }   // n inferred as Int
let names = ["ada", "bob"]
let lens = map(names, fn(s) { len(s) })        // lens: [Int]
```

Every program is type-checked before it runs (gradual: unannotated code is inferred, unknown things are `Any`). Diagnostics have stable codes: T0001 type mismatch, T0002 argument type, T0003 return type, T0004 argument count, T0005 invalid operator (`"a" - 1`), T0006 unknown name (with did-you-mean), T0007 unknown struct field, T0008 unknown module member (`math.sqr`), T0009 missing return, T0010 unreachable code, T0011 non-exhaustive match, T0012 interface not satisfied, T0013 not callable, T0014 Option used as its value, T0015 unknown type, T0016 missing struct field, T0017 assignment to immutable `let`, T0018 used before definition. Default: warnings, the program still runs. `forge run --strict file.fg`: diagnostics are errors, and annotated function arguments/results are also checked at run time (`type error: argument 'n' of 'double' must be Int, got String`).

## Control flow

```forge
let score = 85
if score >= 90 {
    println("A")
} else if score >= 80 {
    println("B")
} else {
    println("C")
}

for i in range(0, 3) {        // 0, 1, 2 (end is exclusive); also: for x in array
    println(i)
}
for e in enumerate(["x", "y"]) {   // enumerate yields { index, value }
    println("{e.index}: {e.value}")
}
for k, v in { a: 1, b: 2 } {       // two-variable form is for objects and maps
    println("{k}={v}")
}

let mut n = 0
while n < 3 {
    n += 1
}

let mut m = 0
loop {
    m += 1
    if m == 2 { continue }
    if m >= 4 { break }
}
println(score > 0 && score < 100)
```

## Functions and closures

```forge
fn add(a, b) {
    return a + b
}

fn greet(name: String) -> String {
    return "Hello, {name}!"
}

let square = fn(x) { return x * x }   // anonymous function

fn make_counter() {
    let mut count = 0
    return fn() {
        count += 1
        return count
    }
}

println(add(2, 3))
println(greet("Ada"))
println(square(4))
let c = make_counter()
c()
println(c())                  // 2
```

Always write an explicit `return`.

## Structs, methods, interfaces

```forge
struct Point {
    x: Int,
    y: Int
}

impl Point {
    fn sum(it) {              // `it` is the receiver (like self)
        return it.x + it.y
    }
}

let p = Point { x: 1, y: 2 }
println(p.sum())

struct User {
    name: String,
    role: String = "member"   // field default
}
let u = User { name: "Ada" }

interface Describable {
    fn describe() -> String
}

impl Describable for User {
    fn describe(it) {
        return it.name + " (" + it.role + ")"
    }
}
println(u.describe())
println(satisfies(u, Describable))
```

## Algebraic types and match

```forge
type Shape = Circle(Float) | Rect(Float, Float)

impl Shape {
    fn area(it) {
        match it {
            Circle(r) => { return 3.14159 * r * r }
            Rect(w, h) => { return w * h }
        }
    }
}

for s in [Circle(1.0), Rect(2.0, 3.0)] {
    println(s.area())
}

match Rect(2.0, 5.0) {
    Circle(r) => println("circle {r}"),
    Rect(w, h) => println("rect {w}x{h}"),
}

let v = 7
match v {
    0 => println("zero"),
    7 => println("seven"),
    _ => println("other"),
}
```

`match` is a statement. Patterns: literals, `_`, bindings, and constructors `Name(a, b)`. There are no guard clauses (`n if ...`) or or-patterns (`1 | 2`).

## Result, Option, errors

```forge
fn parse_age(s) {
    let n = int(s)
    if n < 0 {
        return Err("negative age")
    }
    return Ok(n)
}

fn next_age(s) {
    let n = parse_age(s)?          // ? returns the Err early, unwraps the Ok
    return Ok(n + 1)
}

let good = next_age("41")
if is_ok(good) {
    println("ok {unwrap(good)}")
}
let bad = next_age("-3")
println(is_err(bad))
println(unwrap_or(bad, 0))

let found = Some(3)
println(is_some(found))
println(is_none(None))
match found {
    Some(x) => println("got {x}"),
    None => println("none"),
}

try {
    let z = 1 / 0
} catch e {
    println("caught {e.type}: {e.message}")   // ArithmeticError: division by zero
}
try {
    must Err("bad config")       // must: unwrap or raise
} catch e {
    println(e.message)
}
```

There is no `throw`. Return `Err(...)` and propagate with `?`, or raise with `assert(cond, msg)` / `must expr` (both are catchable). `?` only works on `Result` values; `?` at the top level of a program stops it with `unhandled error: ...`. `safe { ... }` runs a block and swallows its errors.

Error codes: every runtime error has a stable code, the same on both engines (`E0003` undefined name, `E0004` calling a non-function, `E0005` wrong argument count, `E0007` operator on unsupported types, `E0008` division by zero, `E0009` index out of bounds, `E0010` missing key, `E0012` field access on null, `E0013` unknown field, `E0015` bad builtin argument, `E0020` permission denied, ...); type-checker diagnostics are `T0001`–`T0018`. `forge explain E0009` prints an explanation, example and fix; `forge explain` lists all codes. A caught error has `e.code`. For tools: `forge check file.fg` type-checks without running, and `--error-format json` (or `forge check --format json`) prints one `{code, severity, message, file, line, col, hint, phase}` object per diagnostic.

```forge
try {
    let xs = [1, 2, 3]
    println(xs[5])
} catch e {
    println(e.code)          // E0009
}
```

## Modules

```forge
import { double, shout } from "utils.fg"   // selected names
println(double(21))
```

Native plugins (Rust/C shared libraries built with `crates/forge-plugin`): `import native "target/release/libfoo" as foo` then `foo.add(1, 2)`, or `import { add } from native "path/libfoo"`. The platform suffix is added; paths resolve like `.fg` imports. Needs `--allow-ffi` (full trust; denied under `--sandbox` and `forge mcp`). Plugin errors are catchable runtime errors.

`import "utils.fg"` brings every top-level name into scope. Paths resolve relative to the current working directory, then `forge_modules/<name>/main.fg`. Stdlib modules (`math`, `fs`, `http`, ...) are always in scope; never import them. Packages are declared in `forge.toml` (`forge add <pkg>`).

## Collections and builtins

```forge
let nums = [5, 3, 8, 1]
let mut xs = [1, 2]
xs = push(xs, 3)              // portable: reassign the result
println(map(nums, fn(x) { return x * 2 }))
println(filter(nums, fn(x) { return x > 2 }))
println(reduce(nums, 0, fn(acc, x) { return acc + x }))   // (array, initial, fn)
println(sort(nums))
println(sort(nums, fn(a, b) { return b - a }))            // comparator returns a number
println(nums.filter(fn(x) { return x % 2 == 1 }).map(fn(x) { return x * 10 }))
println(find(nums, fn(x) { return x > 4 }))
println(contains(nums, 8))

let mut user = { name: "Ada", age: 36 }
user.email = "ada@example.com"
println(keys(user))
println(get(user, "missing", "default"))
println(pick(user, ["name"]))
println(merge(user, { age: 37 }))

let s = "Hello, World"
println(split(s, ", "))
println(join(["a", "b"], "-"))
println(replace(s, "World", "Forge"))
println(s.upper())
println("  pad  ".trim())
println(starts_with(s, "Hell"))
println(substring(s, 0, 5))
println(contains(s, "lo, W"))

let st = set([1, 2, 2, 3])
println(st.has(2))
let mut m = map()
m = m.set("k", 1)
println(m.get("k"))
println([1, 2, 3, 4].stream().filter(fn(x) { return x > 1 }).take(2).collect())
```

Other builtins: `len`, `range`, `reverse`, `sum`, `any`, `all`, `unique`, `zip(a, b)`, `chunk(arr, n)`, `slice(arr, start, end)`, `has_key`, `flatten`, `min_of`, `max_of`, `values`, `omit`, `entries`, `ends_with`, `index_of`, `slugify`, `uuid()`, `typeof`, `str`, `int`, `float`, `wait(seconds)`, `assert`, `assert_eq`.

## Standard library (always in scope)

| Module | Most-used functions (argument order matters) |
| ------ | -------------------------------------------- |
| `math` | `sqrt(x)`, `pow(b, e)`, `abs`, `max(a, b)`, `min`, `floor`, `ceil`, `round`, `random_int(lo, hi)`, `pi`, `e` |
| `fs` | `read(path)`, `write(path, text)`, `append`, `exists`, `list(dir)`, `remove`, `mkdir`, `copy(src, dst)`, `rename` |
| `json` | `parse(text)`, `stringify(value)` |
| `regex` | `test(text, pattern)`, `find(text, pattern)`, `find_all(text, pattern)`, `replace(text, pattern, repl)`, `split(text, pattern)` — text FIRST |
| `crypto` | `sha256(s)`, `md5(s)`, `base64_encode`, `base64_decode`, `hex_encode`, `hex_decode` |
| `http` | `get(url, opts?)`, `post(url, opts?)`, `put`, `delete`, `patch`, `head`; opts: `{ body, headers, params, timeout, auth }`; response: `{ status, ok, body, json, headers }` |
| `db` | SQLite: `open(path)`, `execute(sql, params?)`, `query(sql, params?)` → array of objects, `close()` |
| `pg`, `mysql` | `connect(url)`, `query(conn, sql, params?)`, `execute(conn, sql, params?)`, `close(conn)`; mysql adds `begin/commit/rollback` |
| `jwt` | `sign(claims, secret, opts?)`, `verify(token, secret)`, `decode(token)`, `valid(token, secret)` |
| `csv` | `parse(text)`, `stringify(rows)`, `read(path)`, `write(path, rows)` |
| `env` | `get(name, default?)`, `set`, `has`, `keys` |
| `log` | `info`, `warn`, `error`, `debug` (structured, via tracing) |
| `term` | `red`, `green`, `bold`, `table(rows)`, `bar`, `sparkline`, `banner`, `box` |
| `time` | `now()`, `format`, `parse`, `add`, `diff`, `unix`, `sleep` |
| `os`, `path` | `os.platform()`, `os.cpus()`; `path.join(a, b)`, `path.extname(p)`, `path.basename(p)` |
| `io` | `prompt`, `args_parse`, `args_get`, `args_has` |

`fetch(url)` is shorthand for `http.get`. Shell builtins: `sh(cmd)`, `sh_lines`, `sh_ok`, `sh_json`, `run_command`, `pipe_to(data, cmd)` (need `--allow-run`).

```forge
println(math.sqrt(16.0))
println(regex.find_all("a1b22c333", "\\d+"))
println(regex.replace("a1b2", "\\d", "#"))
println(json.stringify({ a: [1, 2] }))
println(json.parse("[1, 2]")[1])
println(env.get("FORGE_LLMS_UNSET", "fallback"))
println(path.join("a", "b.txt"))
fs.write("/tmp/forge_llms_demo.txt", "line1\nline2")
println(fs.read("/tmp/forge_llms_demo.txt"))
fs.remove("/tmp/forge_llms_demo.txt")
let tok = jwt.sign({ uid: 1 }, "secret")
println(jwt.verify(tok, "secret").uid)
```

## Concurrency

```forge
// Structured concurrency: all spawns join before the block ends; results in spawn order
let results = squad {
    spawn { 1 + 1 }
    spawn { 2 + 2 }
}
println(results)              // [2, 4]

let h = spawn { 40 + 2 }      // detached task
println(await h)
println(await_all([spawn { 1 }, spawn { 2 }]))

let ch = channel()            // unbounded; channel(n) is bounded
spawn {
    send(ch, "ping")
    send(ch, "pong")
}
println(receive(ch))
println(receive(ch))

let t = spawn {
    wait(1)
    return "late"
}
println(await_timeout(t, 10))  // null on timeout (milliseconds)
```

Also: `try_send`, `try_receive`, `select(channels, timeout_ms?)`, `close(ch)`.

Tasks communicate through return values (`squad` results, `await`) and channels. Do not mutate captured variables from inside `spawn` and expect the parent to see it: the default VM gives each task its own copy (the `--interp` engine shares closure state).

## HTTP server

```forge
@server(port: 8080)

@get("/hello/:name")
fn hello(name: String) -> Json {
    return { greeting: "Hello, {name}!" }
}

@get("/search")
fn search(query) -> Json {
    return { q: query.q }
}

@post("/echo")
fn echo(body: Json) -> Json {
    return { received: body }
}
```

Handler parameters bind by name: path params (`:name`), `body`/`data` (parsed JSON body), `query`/`qs` (all query params), or a single query param by its name. Return an object to send JSON. Decorators: `@server(port:, host:, cors:)`, `@get`, `@post`, `@put`, `@delete`, `@ws`. The server binds `127.0.0.1` by default with same-origin CORS (`cors: "permissive"` to open it). Each request runs in an isolated fork, so handler mutations of top-level variables do not persist across requests. Server programs run on the bytecode VM by default (`forge --interp run` serves on the interpreter; responses are identical). Unknown decorators or non-literal `@server` arguments make the program fall back to the interpreter automatically.

## Tests

Put `@test fn test_name() { assert_eq(1 + 1, 2) }` functions in `tests/*.fg` and run `forge test` (`forge --allow-run test` if tests use the shell).

## MCP tools (forge mcp serve)

`forge mcp serve tools.fg` serves the file's `@tool` functions to AI agents over the Model Context Protocol. Parameter types become the JSON Schema (`Int` integer, `Float` number, `String`, `Bool`, `[T]` array, `Object`/`Map<String, T>` object, a struct object, `?T`/`Option<T>` or a default make it optional); the return type becomes the output schema (`Result<T, E>` describes `T`).

```
struct Report { city: String, temp_c: Float }

@tool(description: "Weather for a city (sample data)", read_only: true)
@param(city: "City name")
fn weather(city: String, unit: String = "C") -> Result<Report, String> {
    if city == "Oslo" { return Ok(Report { city: "Oslo", temp_c: -3.0 }) }
    return Err("unknown city: " + city)
}

@resource(uri: "weather://cities", description: "Known cities")
fn cities() { return ["Oslo"] }
```

`@tool` needs a description (`@tool("...")` also works); optional `name`, `title`, `timeout` (seconds), `read_only`, `destructive`, `idempotent`, `open_world`. `@param(name: "doc", ...)` documents parameters. Decorator arguments must be constants. Return `Err(msg)` for a tool error. The top level runs once at start-up; each call runs in a fresh sandboxed fork of it (deny-all plus the server's `--allow-*` grants, `--max-time`), so calls never share state. With plain `forge mcp`, `run_forge` takes an optional `session_id` that keeps top-level variables between calls; `reset_session` clears it.

## Common mistakes

- `let {a, b} = obj` does not parse. Use `unpack {a, b} from obj` or `unpack [x, ...rest] from arr`; `let (a, b) = tuple` works for tuples.
- `for i, x in array` does not work. Use `for e in enumerate(array) { e.index, e.value }`.
- No `|x| ...` closures and no arrow functions. Write `fn(x) { return ... }`.
- No `throw`, no `elif`, no `??` operator. Use `Err`/`?`, `else if`, and `get(obj, key, default)`.
- Method chains cannot start a line with `.`; keep `a.filter(...).map(...)` on one line.
- `regex.*` takes `(text, pattern)`, not `(pattern, text)`. Escape backslashes in patterns: `"\\d+"`.
- `reduce(array, initial, fn)` — the initial value comes second.
- Mutating a field or index requires a `let mut` binding.
- `trim`/`upper`/`lower` are methods (`s.trim()`). `wait(n)` takes seconds; `await_timeout`/`select` take milliseconds.
- Shell builtins need `forge --allow-run run`. The HTTP client refuses private/loopback hosts unless `FORGE_HTTP_ALLOW_PRIVATE=1`.
- Always pass user input to SQL as a params array: `db.query("... WHERE id = ?", [id])`.

## Engine notes (v0.9.x)

The default bytecode VM and the reference interpreter run the full Forge test suite identically; `cargo test --test engine_diff` gates every example and fixture on both. Programs the VM compiler cannot handle fall back to the interpreter automatically; `@server` programs are served by the VM. Force the interpreter with `forge --interp run`.
